sections.text: When a flight is disrupted, every minute counts. What if every disruption you'd already solved could help solve the next one?
Operations desks handle disruptions every day. Systems keep the records, but not the judgement: what actually worked last time.
Meet the IROPS Disruption Memory Agent. Every resolved disruption becomes precedent for the next one.
Here's the console. Flight ZZ1137: a hundred and ninety minutes late, twenty-three passengers misconnecting.
One click: the agent embeds the case, finds similar past disruptions, and Nova Lite proposes a plan that cites its precedents.
Code checks the plan too: stranded passengers left uncovered are flagged before anyone approves.
Open a precedent to see what the desk did last time, and how it turned out. Mixed results come back too, with what went wrong.
Nothing executes automatically. Each action is a proposal a person approves, edits or rejects, and every decision is recorded.
Every run is logged: the model, here Amazon Nova Lite, its token counts and latency, and the exact cases it retrieved.
This loop is the heart of the product. Each disruption becomes a summary and an embedding. Similar resolved cases are retrieved, the agent proposes, and a person decides.
Record the outcome, and it's written with its embedding in the same transaction that turns the case into precedent. Search for a similar weather disruption now, and ZZ1137 comes back.
Even rejected proposals are kept. Unlike a chatbot, what it recommends tomorrow depends on what it recorded today.
You can also question the memory in plain English. Nova Lite writes the SQL and runs it through CockroachDB's managed MCP server, read-only by the app's own guardrails.
The answer arrives with the query and the rows behind it: weather, at 3.45.
Under the hood, records and embeddings live in one CockroachDB database and commit in the same transaction: no sync job, no drift.
A case-status prefix on the vector index filters to resolved cases inside the index itself.
On AWS, Bedrock provides Titan embeddings and Nova Lite reasoning, Lambda runs the agent, and S3 serves the console, scaling to zero when idle.
Every disruption handled today makes the next one easier to handle.
